name: Catherby
tagline: An agentic operating system for a farm's back office
description: Franco and I weren't planning another startup. We were building software for clients when we met a farmer who wanted more time in the field and less time in the office. His records were spread across spreadsheets, paper and WhatsApp. We thought agents could work with the documents he already had, without giving him another system to learn. That became Catherby. Farmers send invoices, photos and voice notes; the agents record purchases, track costs and stock, check grain settlements and prepare what needs to go out for the owner's approval. I build the web app, backend and agents. We're starting with crop farms in Argentina.

name: Verelyn
tagline: Journalist agents that write your morning briefing
description: The newsletters you pay for are good, and they were written for thousands of people at once, which is why most of them sit unopened. Verelyn is a newsroom built around one reader. Its journalist agents read your sources every morning, fold four reports of the same thing into a single event with its sources attached, weigh each one against what you actually have riding on this week, and send one briefing at 07:00. Every item is signed by the agent who wrote it and carries its sources, including where they disagree. Most events get dropped and the reason is recorded, so a miss can be answered for. Hayes covers the first beat, startups and AI. I built it in August 2026 and brought on paying readers.

name: Flare
description: A voice-based social app I built and launched on iOS. Friends shared moments from their lives, and AI turned those moments into conversations and briefings to help them keep up with each other. I built the app and backend with Expo, React Native and Supabase. We paused development in July 2026: it had users but no revenue, and our mining income was no longer enough to keep funding it. That experience changed how we approached Catherby. We asked for a customer's commitment to pay before writing any code.

name: Privé
description: Creators sell digital content, video calls and VIP group access without leaving Telegram. They get paid through Mercado Pago, crypto or bank transfer, and the money lands in their account, never mine. Privé charges 0% on every plan and every method, and makes its money on the Premium subscription instead of a cut of each sale. Bot, mini app, payment rails and the fee engine are all mine. I stopped actively developing it in September 2026, but it continues to bring in new paying subscribers.

name: Inception Crypto
tagline: Built and hosted cryptocurrency mining farms
description: Started this at 21 with friends, first with Ethereum rigs and later Bitcoin equipment. We built and hosted mining farms for customers, growing to around 150 ASIC miners. I handled sales, customer relationships and finances; Franco led the technical setup and operations. Income from the business supported us while we worked on our later software projects. We ran it from September 2020 to July 2026.

name: Stevay
description: A construction company's data is scattered across ERPs, spreadsheets and WhatsApp, and none of it lines up until the year closes. Stevay sat on top and read it as it arrived, then structured the administrative work and ran it: 75+ agents across finances, documentation, purchasing, progress, certification, management and communication. Nothing new to adopt, and a human signed off on anything that touched money. I co-founded it with Franco Quattroqui and owned tech and product. We shipped it, then stopped taking it forward.

name: DL3ARN
description: We built a SaaS to make academic credentials verifiable on-chain. Great team, real leads from universities, a product that worked. Then the crypto bear market hit and made fundraising impossible. I learned more from this one than from anything that succeeded.

name: Clikan
description: A mobile app where you collect and share real-world spots. Taught me everything about social mechanics, location APIs, and thinking mobile-first. The product didn't survive, but the lessons did.

name: Aequsy
description: A platform where you could win prizes while supporting real causes. I got deep into payments, conversion funnels, and building for a mission bigger than the product itself.

name: Bloorfy
description: My first real coding project. I built it to learn web development and ended up learning what it actually takes to ship something. Messy code, zero users, but it changed my trajectory.
